question.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
question.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
question.clue: Despite not being native to it, the Phanariotes served as administrators of a region on this river.

swap.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
swap.clue: Italy invaded this country during World War II when it was ruled by a man who claimed descent from Skanderbeg.

question.leadin: In an unprecedented decision, the Constitutional Court of this country annulled its electoral results in December 2024.
question.text: Name this Eastern European country where far-right parties protested the annulment from Bucharest.
question.clue: A dictator of this country who styled himself as "Conducator" ("con-doo-kuh-TOR") put down a rebellion led by Horia Sima, the Legionnaires' rebellion.

swap.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
swap.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

question.leadin: This politician was overthrown in a revolt that began at Timisoara.
question.text: Name this communist politician who succeeded Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej and built the Centrul Civic.
question.clue: This man outlined seventeen proposals inspired by China's Cultural Revolution in his July Theses, and his Decree 770 banned abortions in his country.

swap.text: This eventual assassin of Franz Ferdinand was unable to act after the initial failure by Cabrinovic. He was imprisoned and eventually died of tuberculosis in his cell.
swap.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

question.leadin: This man's forces executed thousands of prisoners of war handed over by the British in the Bleiburg Repatriations.
question.text: Name this man who led a successful anti-Axis resistance movement as leader of the Partisans. This leader later served as the first chairman of the Non-Aligned Movement, of which his country was a founding member.
question.clue: This man's falling out with a political ally foiled his plans to annex Trieste.

swap.text: As a result of the last Russo-Turkish War, this country gained autonomy from Ottoman rule. Boris III was a tsar of this modern-day nation, whose capital city is Sofia.
swap.clue: This country pursued the Treaty of Craiova to recover territory lost in the Treaty of Neuilly, its "second national catastrophe," which saw it lose Southern Dobruja.

question.leadin: The independence of this country was championed by its national hero Skanderbeg.
question.text: Identify this modern-day country, whose twentieth century rulers include Ismail Qemali, Ramiz Alia, and one king, Zog I.
question.clue: This home of Skanderbeg was ruled by the isolationist Enver Hoxha.

swap.text: In 1938, he married Geraldine Apponyi, a postcard saleswoman at the Budapest National Museum. After World War II, he abdicated following the Communist takeover led by Enver Hoxha. For 15 points-name this Albanian leader who had declared himself king in 1928.
swap.clue: He went into exile after Italy overran his country in 1939, abandoning the republican government he had formed in 1922.

question.text: An army of these people had 199 out of every 200 eyes removed after they were defeated by the Byzantines at the Battle of Kleidion. This ethnic group was subjugated by the Byzantine emperor Basil II.
question.clue: Many members of this ethnicity were killed by bashi-bazouk (BYE-jee-buh-ZOOK) soldiers during the April Uprising in namesake "horrors."

swap.leadin: Hadzi Prodan attempted to lead a revolt between this nation's two major uprisings, and its foundation is closely tied to a document simply known as The Proclamation.
swap.text: Name this Balkan nation whose independence movement was led by Karadorde Petrovich, or Black George, and Milos Obrenovich.
swap.clue: This state was governed by a code named for its "Mighty" king Stefan Dusan .

question.leadin: Answer the following about the hit Serbian propaganda song "God is a Serb," sometimes erroneously called "Serbia Strong."
question.text: "God is a Serb" refers to Croats as members of this fascist organization. Founded by Ante Pavelic, it collaborated with German and Italian occupiers and nominally ruled Croatia during World War II.
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: After the War of Chioggia, Venice lost control of Ragusa, which later became a major trading republic in this region. To repay its debt to Venice, the Fourth Crusade sacked Zadar, a city in this region on the eastern Adriatic coast.

question.leadin: Napoleon proclaimed Marshal Auguste de Marmont as "Duke of [this place]" after he annexed it to the Kingdom of Italy.
question.text: Name this merchant republic centered at the port of Dubrovnik in modern-day Croatia.
question.clue: This republic along the eastern coast of the Adriatic. The modern name of its capital is Dubrovnik.

swap.leadin: This country's war of independence began a year after the Log Revolution and included the Vukovar massacre.
swap.text: Name this country that carried out Operation Storm, resulting in the defeat of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.
swap.clue: A water tower riddled with bullets in this country's independence war was preserved in Vukovar.

question.leadin: This man helped put down a peasant revolt in Galati in 1907, and once in power executed high level dignitaries at Jilava Prison.
question.text: Identify this prime minister under King Carol II who allied his country with the Nazis during World War II.

swap.leadin: Name some fields in European history which have really cool names.
swap.text: The Serbian prince Lazar was crushed at this field during the Battle of Kosovo in 1389, while Milos Obilic got some revenge by stabbing Murad I.

question.text: Unfortunately for Murad, he was assassinated by this Serbian national hero toward the end of that very same Battle of Kosovo.
question.clue: According to tradition, this was the name of the Serbian soldier that assassinated the sultan Murad. He is venerated as a saint in the Serbian church and is celebrated in the epic poem The Mountain Wreath.

swap.leadin: A king of this country controversially married Queen Draga, the former widow of an engineer. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this modern day country that witnessed the Slaughter of the Knezes in 1804 and the assassination of King Alexander I in 1903.
swap.clue: A leader of a secret society in this country codenamed "Apis" orchestrated the murder of its king Alexander and its queen Draga in 1903.
